lemma: Window bookkeeping (conditional). Let N = 2^n, threshold s = N^beta, and suppose CC(MCSP[N^beta]) <= C0*N^theta. Suppose a simulation L(f) <= C*CC(f)^q holds for the MMW-derived families. Then every probabilistic formula for MCSP[N^beta] has size <= C*C0^q*N^(q*theta). CJW20 Thm 1.6 (verbatim from the ledger source check: for every alpha in (0,1) and eps>0, MCSP[n^alpha] has no probabilistic n^(2+alpha-eps)-size formulas) gives size >= N^(2+beta-eps). The two bounds contradict iff q*theta < 2+beta-eps. Necessary condition: theta < (2+beta)/q as eps -> 0.

proved_step: Depth-leaf bound (restricted, shrinks G0001). Let C be a fan-in-2 DAG over inputs x_1..x_n with s gates and depth d (inputs have depth 0). Its full unfolding, the tree obtained by duplicating every shared node, is a formula F_C computing the same function, and F_C has at most 2^d leaves. Proof by induction on depth: an input has 1 = 2^0 leaf; a gate v of depth k has inputs a,b of depth at most k-1, so L(v) = L(a)+L(b) <= 2*2^(k-1) = 2^k. Corollary: if d <= c*log2(s) then |F_C| <= s^c, a fixed-exponent simulation. Scope: this is the only fixed-q case proved here; it covers depth O(log s) only and does NOT close G0001, since MMW-derived families have depth poly(s).

proved_step: Reduction of G0001 to (D). Let a, c >= 1 be constants and B a fixed binary basis. If every f with CC_B(f) = s has a fan-in-2 B-circuit of size s' <= s^a and depth d' <= c*log2(s'), then L_B(f) <= s^(a*c) for all such f, i.e. a fixed-q simulation L(f) <= C*CC(f)^q with q = a*c and C = 1.
derivation: Take a minimal circuit C for f, |C| = s. Apply (D) to get C' with s' <= s^a gates and depth d' <= c*log2(s'). S0002 gives that the full unfolding F_{C'} computes f and has at most 2^{d'} leaves. Then 2^{d'} <= s'^c <= s^(a*c), and formula size equals leaf count, so L_B(f) <= s^(a*c). proved_step: Restricted fan-out bound (shrinks G0001, does not close it). Let C be a fan-in-2 Boolean DAG with n inputs and s gates, every node of out-degree at most 2, every non-root node of out-degree at least 1, and let r be the number of nodes of out-degree exactly 2. Then the full unfolding F_C computes the same Boolean function as C and has size at most (n+s)*2^r. Corollary: if r <= c*log2(s) then |F_C| <= (n+s)*s^c. PROOF: For a node u let P(u) be the set of directed paths from u to the root. The unfolding has exactly |P(u)| copies of u, so |F_C| = sum_u |P(u)| <= (n+s)*max_u |P(u)|. Let R be the set of out-degree-2 nodes, |R| = r. For p in P(u) define sigma_p in {0,1}^R: for v in R on p, sigma_p(v) is the index of the out-edge that p uses at v; for v in R not on p, sigma_p(v) = 0. Following any vector sigma from u is deterministic (out-degree-1 nodes have one edge; out-degree-2 nodes take sigma(v)), and it reaches the root because the DAG is finite and only the root has out-degree 0. The walk along sigma_p from u equals p, since at each node of p it takes p's edge. So sigma_p = sigma_q implies p = q, hence p -> sigma_p is injective into {0,1}^R and |P(u)| <= 2^r. Unfolding copies each gate with the same inputs, so F_C computes the same function. Multi-edges are handled by indexing the two edges of a gate. QED. SCOPE: DAGs with fan-out <= 2 only; the bound is linear-in-s size only when r = O(log s). It does not bound fan-out-2 chains (r = s). Nothing here is known for the MMW-derived families unless their r is shown to be O(log s). Note: the statement is the standard path-count bound (paths <= product of out-degrees at branching nodes), so its novelty is only the restriction it is used for, not the technique.
